name: Oscar Health, Inc.
blurb: Oscar Health is a technology-oriented health insurer that operates exclusively on the Affordable Care Act individual marketplace — the government-subsidized exchange where Americans who lack employer-sponsored coverage shop for plans. Founded in 2012, it built a reputation for a cleaner app and lighter administrative friction than legacy insurers, but spent years losing money as it learned the brutal actuarial realities of insuring a volatile, cost-heavy population.
recent: Oscar reached 2.0 million members by end of 2025, with roughly 93% of premiums flowing through government advance tax credits — a financial structure that makes it exquisitely sensitive to ACA subsidy policy. Medical costs rose faster than expected in 2025, driving a quarterly operating loss of ~$129 million. For 2026 the company has raised premiums by roughly 28% year-over-year and projected membership growth of ~58% alongside a return to operating profitability. The fate of enhanced ACA subsidies — debated in Congress — is its single largest macro risk: the company estimates a 20–30% market contraction if subsidies lapse.
